_about: AI check for jobs the rules leave unclear (needs_review). The model must give an exact quote; the code checks the quote is really on the page before the job's status changes. `enabled` controls the daily run only: `jobhunter check` works either way. See src/jobhunter/ai_check.py.
_model: The first step. deepseek-* (DEEPSEEK_API_KEY, about $0.01 a job): code fetches the job's own links and its Greenhouse/Lever/Ashby posting, DeepSeek reads them; it cannot search the web. claude-code: the Claude Code CLI with web search on your Claude login, for every job. claude-* (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY): the API with its own web search, about $0.10-0.30 a job with claude-opus-5-5.
_web_model: With a deepseek-* model: jobs it could not settle (no verdict, or its quote not found on a page) go here. claude-code or claude-code:sonnet runs the Claude Code CLI with WebSearch and WebFetch on your Claude login, so no API bill; about a minute a job. Code fetches the page it quotes and checks the quote there. Empty: DeepSeek only.
_max_jobs_per_run: A cap per daily run. The rest wait for the next run or `jobhunter check`.
_lookback_days: The daily run checks unchecked jobs from today and the days before, newest first, up to max_jobs_per_run, so a busy day's leftovers are checked on a later run.
_find_dates: Before the check: undated needs_review jobs (Google Jobs often gives no date) get their posting date from the schema.org datePosted on their own pages, else from web_model searching the web; code finds the quote on the page and reads the date from it. Then the age rule judges them. See src/jobhunter/posted_date.py and `jobhunter dates`.
_max_fetches_per_job: Pages code fetches for DeepSeek (and the Claude API may open).
_max_page_tokens: Claude API only: how much of each fetched page is read.
